name: Limassol
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Limassol | Ship UTM
description: Thickness measurement for Limassol ship managers and ships at Limassol port or anchorage: CAP and renewal survey gauging, takeover and scrubber piping UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging in Limassol for Ships and Ship Managers
intro: Limassol is one of the largest third-party ship-management centres anywhere, and many of the technical managers who plan gauging for ships all over the world work within a short distance of each other here. Ships themselves call at Limassol port and anchorage for cargo, crew changes, stores and bunkers, giving short but usable windows for gauging. We mobilise a team from India to vessels at Limassol, and can plan gauging for Limassol-managed ships wherever their next docking falls.

highlights.p: Fleet managers, technical superintendents and crewing departments for very large third-party fleets work in Limassol. A gauging plan agreed here can be carried out on a ship in Cyprus waters or at the port of its next docking.

Ships call at the Limassol anchorage for crew changes, stores, bunkers and orders. A day or two at anchor is enough for deck, hatch cover and selected ballast tank readings when spaces are prepared in advance.
Offshore support vessels linked to gas exploration off Cyprus call at Limassol between jobs. Their decks, tanks and piping can be gauged during port stays between charters or at a change of contract.

port.h: Limassol: Cyprus's main port and its ship-management centre
p: Limassol is the main cargo port of the Republic of Cyprus. Since the port was concessioned, the container terminal has been run by Eurogate, the multipurpose terminal by DP World and marine services by P&O Maritime, with the Cyprus Ports Authority remaining the landlord. The port handles containers, general and project cargo, cruise calls and offshore supply work, and the anchorage off the port is busy with ships calling for crew changes, stores, bunkers and orders while trading between Suez, the Levant, the Black Sea and Europe.

What sets Limassol apart is ashore. Over several decades the city has become one of the largest third-party ship-management centres anywhere, providing technical, crewing and commercial management for fleets of tankers, bulk carriers, container ships, gas carriers and offshore vessels owned by investors from Europe, Asia and beyond. The Cyprus ship management cluster means that a large share of the decisions about gauging, docking scope and steel renewal for ships trading worldwide are taken in Limassol, even though few of those ships ever dock in Cyprus. A superintendent here may be planning a renewal survey in China one week and a CAP programme in Turkey the next.

That shapes inspection demand at the port itself. Ships calling at Limassol tend to be on short stays, so gauging here is usually targeted: a superintendent driving down to the port to attend a crew-change call, wanting deck, hatch, ballast tank or piping readings to settle a specific question before the next survey or a charter. Takeover gauging also arises. When a ship moves into third-party management, the incoming manager often wants a measured condition baseline, and a Cyprus call is a convenient place to take it because the people who will own the results can attend the same day. For ship managers in Limassol, the port is also the easiest place to see a ship's condition first-hand before committing to a docking scope.

facilities.h: Where we gauge ships at Limassol
p: At the port, gauging is done on container ships at the Eurogate terminal, on general cargo, project and offshore vessels at the multipurpose berths, and occasionally on cruise ships during turnaround calls. All work alongside is subject to the terminal's ISPS and safety rules and is arranged through the ship's agent. At the anchorage the practical limits are sea state and the ship's own programme: if a ship is bunkering or changing crew, tank entry has to be planned around those operations, and spaces should be ventilated and certified safe before the stay begins if the window is short.

Cyprus has no ship-repair yard on the scale of those in Greece or Turkey, so heavy steel renewal on Cyprus-managed ships is done abroad, whether in Greece, Turkey, the Middle East, China or elsewhere. Gauging in Limassol therefore works best as preparation: readings taken at anchor or alongside give the technical manager a measured steel estimate to send to yards, and can be followed by in-dock gauging at the chosen yard if our team can reach it in time. Thickness gauging in Cyprus is, in practice, the first half of a docking plan rather than the whole of it.
list: Eurogate container terminal, Limassol port — ballast tank, deck and scrubber piping checks on container ships during terminal stays
Multipurpose berths, Limassol port — gauging of holds, decks and tanks on general cargo, project cargo and offshore support vessels
Limassol anchorage — targeted gauging during crew-change, stores and bunker calls, reached by launch arranged through the agent
Cruise calls at Limassol port — tank and void space gauging on cruise ships where the call and the ship's programme allow access
Vasilikos energy port east of Limassol — deck, piping and ballast space gauging on tankers within terminal rules, combined with a Limassol job

context.h: Regulatory and management context in Cyprus
p: Cyprus is an EU member state and belongs to both the Paris MoU and the Mediterranean MoU on port state control. The Cyprus flag is one of the main EU registries, and many Cyprus-managed ships fly it alongside Liberian, Marshall Islands, Maltese and other flags. EU ETS has covered shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, and both apply to voyages calling at Cypriot ports. Around the island, the Mediterranean SOx ECA has applied since 1 May 2025. On scrubber-fitted ships, the wash-water and overboard lines are a recurring inspection item, because years of open-loop service tend to show up there first.

The management model matters for gauging. In third-party management, the manager acts for an owner who may be a fund, a bank-backed company or a family shipping group, and steel renewal or a CAP programme needs the owner's approval. That puts a premium on clear, well-organised data: a steel renewal estimate by area, readings that can be compared directly with the last class report, and photographs that let the owner understand the condition without boarding. Takeovers, sales and changes of manager each generate their own condition-gauging work, and a Limassol desk is usually where that work is commissioned.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Limassol
jobs.p: Limassol jobs are usually short and targeted, set up by a manager who already knows which question the readings must answer. A typical brief names the spaces, the window at anchor or alongside, and the decision at stake: dock now or later, buy or walk away, take the ship into management or not. We plan the scope around that question rather than around a full survey extent.
list: Takeover gauging on a bulk carrier joining a Limassol-managed fleet, measuring holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks during a crew-change call at anchor to set a condition baseline.
Pre-docking gauging on a product tanker at the Limassol anchorage, giving the manager a measured steel estimate to send to yards in Greece and Turkey ahead of its renewal survey.
Gauging for CAP on a chemical tanker managed from Limassol, starting with deck and ballast tanks during a Cyprus call and completed at the docking yard.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping inspection on a container ship at the Eurogate terminal after a leak alarm at sea.
Deck, tank and piping gauging on an offshore support vessel in port between charters, ahead of the next charterer's inspection.

logistics: The team flies into Larnaca International Airport, the island's main gateway, or Paphos International Airport, and reaches Limassol by road. Port passes under ISPS for the Eurogate and multipurpose terminals, and launches for the anchorage, are arranged through the ship's agent, with crew lists, certificates and equipment details sent ahead. Indian nationals need a visa to enter Cyprus, so we confirm the current entry route for each technician when the job is scoped and start the application as soon as the call looks likely. Short anchorage calls are the ones that most need this early start.

faqs.q: Our ship calls at Limassol for a crew change only. Can gauging still be useful?
faqs.a: Yes, if the scope matches the window. In a stay of a day or so we can usually cover deck plating, hatch covers or coamings, and one or two ballast tanks that the crew has opened, ventilated and certified safe before arrival. That is enough to answer a specific question, such as whether a known corroded area has advanced, even if it is not a full survey extent.

faqs.q: Can you plan gauging from Limassol for a ship docking outside Cyprus?
faqs.a: Yes. Much of the planning for Cyprus-managed ships happens in Limassol while the ship is elsewhere. We can agree the scope with the technical department, review previous thickness reports and class records, and mobilise the team from India to the docking port, provided the yard is somewhere our technicians can obtain visas and access in time.

faqs.q: Can you provide a takeover condition baseline for a ship joining our management?
faqs.a: Yes. A takeover baseline usually covers the structure the incoming manager will be answerable for: holds or cargo tanks where accessible, ballast tanks, deck, hatch covers and key piping systems. We compare the readings with the last thickness report on record, so you can see what has changed since the previous renewal survey and plan the first docking under your management with the facts in hand.

faqs.q: Do you gauge offshore support vessels in Limassol?
faqs.a: Yes. Offshore vessels between charters are a good fit, because tanks and decks are usually accessible during a port stay. We measure cargo deck plating where equipment and pipe are handled, mud, brine, fuel and water tanks once cleaned and certified, ballast tanks and sea water piping, and report in a form the next charterer's inspector can follow.
